note: Anti-NGF antibodies reached IC/BPS on chemical-cystitis rodent models; a small tanezumab POC was positive, the dose-ranging trial was stopped for futility, and ASP6294 later missed too.
label: IC/BPS (anti-NGF)

engagement.model: Chemical cystitis in rats/mice with NGF sequestration
engagement.note: Bladder NGF drove hyper-reflexia in rats and sequestration blocked it; no IC trial reported an NGF or bladder-reflex readout of target engagement.
engagement.short: Rat bladder NGF; no patient PD
engagement.quote: Administration of exogenous nerve growth factor into the lumen of the urinary bladders of normal anaesthetized rats produced a rapid and marked bladder hyper-reflexia similar to that seen with experimental inflammation.
engagement.confidence_note: Patient trials read from abstracts and registry records; ASP6294's EU CTR results list no PD endpoint despite PD in the title.
engagement.reason: No engagement readout in IC trials
engagement.judgement: Evans 2011 found no change in micturition frequency or voided volume (the rat cystometry readouts' nearest human counterparts) but did see fewer urgency episodes; these are symptom endpoints, not a PD readout of NGF binding, so not scored as engagement.

dose.model: Chemical cystitis in rats/mice with NGF sequestration
dose.note: trkA-IgG 1 mg/kg set no human exposure target; no source bridges the cystitis models to tanezumab's IC doses (200 µg/kg IV; 1–20 mg SC) or ASP6294's 320 mg SC.
dose.short: No model exposure target for IC
dose.quote: Treatment of animals with the fusion molecule at 1 mg/kg, immediately before inflammation of the bladder, largely, and very significantly, prevented the expected increases in reflex excitability of this organ.
dose.confidence_note: Absence of an exposure bridge is a negative search over abstracts, registry records and the 2012 AdCom briefing.
dose.judgement: Hu 2005 (REN1820 in CYP cystitis, doi:10.1097/01.ju.0000155170.15023.e5) also reports a fixed dose only; none of the cystitis models dosed a member drug, so no member exposure was stated to compare.

efficacy.model: Chemical cystitis in rats/mice with NGF sequestration
efficacy.note: Irritant cystitis in rats: trkA-IgG prevented and partly reversed bladder hyper-reflexia; later CYP-cystitis work with REN1820 agreed.
efficacy.quote: Systemic treatment with the nerve growth factor-sequestering molecule, but not control molecules, partially and significantly reversed established inflammatory changes, by about 30-60%, depending on outcome measure.
efficacy.judgement: Model family chosen as the NGF-sequestration cystitis work the class rested on (Dmitrieva 1997; Hu 2005, doi:10.1097/01.ju.0000155170.15023.e5). None dosed tanezumab, fulranumab or ASP6294, hence product_in_model false. Opens the chem-cystitis x tanezumab x iv track (Evans 2011 single IV dose).

efficacy.model: Chemical cystitis in rats/mice with NGF sequestration
efficacy.note: A single tanezumab 200 µg/kg IV dose cut average daily IC pain 1.4 points more than placebo at week 6 (n=64), the primary endpoint.
efficacy.short: Tanezumab POC cut IC pain 1.4 points
efficacy.quote: At week 6 tanezumab produced a significant reduction from baseline in average daily pain score vs placebo (treatment difference [LS mean, 90% CI] was -1.4 [-2.2, -0.5]).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract only; NCT00601484 registry results (posted 2021-05-13) give LS mean difference -1.36, 90% CI -2.203 to -0.510.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by us: Evans does not set the rodent data beside the trial in its abstract. Direction only, as the rat readouts (reflex excitability) and the human endpoint (NRS pain) are not on one scale.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: sign of change in bladder pain / hyper-reflexia vs control

efficacy.model: Chemical cystitis in rats/mice with NGF sequestration
efficacy.note: Tanezumab's 205-patient SC dose-ranging IC trial (1-20 mg q8w), given on top of standard of care in both arms, was stopped for futility.
efficacy.short: Larger tanezumab IC trial stopped for futility
efficacy.quote: A second study in patients with interstitial cystitis was impacted by the clinical hold and terminated for futility.
efficacy.confidence_note: Sponsor briefing for the 2012 FDA Arthritis Advisory Committee; the per-arm numbers come from the later registry posting.
efficacy.judgement: Track chem-cystitis x tanezumab x sc; the IV POC (entry 2) is its own track, so no carry-over. Design: tanezumab or placebo added to standard of care in both arms, scored on the trial's primary endpoint like any other trial; combination_with null because no named partner drug was given against a control. Year 2012, the first public statement of futility; NCT00999518 results (posted 2021-08-03) show week-8 differences vs placebo of -0.03 to -0.23, all 95% CIs crossing zero. Fulranumab (Wang 2017) and ASP6294 (EudraCT 2016-004138-12) now have their own tracks (entries 7 and 9). Nickel 2016 pooled analysis reports a benefit in women only, treated as post hoc. The track has no separate 1997 opener: appending one after this 2012 entry would break year order; it opens with entry 1's model first use.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: sign of change in bladder pain vs placebo

patient_trials.quote: This study was terminated on 16 November 2010 following a US FDA partial clinical hold for the tanezumab interstitial cystitis clinical study announced on 19 July 2010 for potential safety issues, and following a pre-planned interim analysis.

Women with interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome and patients with symptoms suggesting the concomitant presence of nonurological associated somatic syndromes were more likely to experience significant pain reduction with tanezumab than with placebo therapy.

efficacy.confidence_note: Full text searched (PMC9721442): no bladder or cystitis model. model_first_use_year 2016 is a proxy from the IC trial's EudraCT number (2016-004138-12); the paper is dated later.
efficacy.note: ASP6294 (PEGylated Fab') relieved pain in adjuvant-arthritis mice and MIA-arthritis rats like an anti-NGF IgG; no bladder model reported.
efficacy.quote: The anti-NGF PEGylated Fab' showed specific binding to and biological inhibitory activity against NGF, and analgesic effects in adjuvant-induced arthritis model mice in a similar manner to an anti-NGF IgG.
efficacy.judgement: ASP6294 went into IC patients on Astellas's own arthritis pain models, not the draft's NGF-sequestration cystitis models, so it is its own track; prediction is class-level analgesia.
efficacy.model: ASP6294 (PEG-Fab') vs anti-NGF IgG in adjuvant-arthritis mice and MIA-arthritis rats

efficacy.magnitude_basis: sign of pain change vs control (rodent arthritis pain vs IC/BPS daily pain NRS)
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry record read (results first posted 2020-02-08); the model paper was public 2022-12-02 (PMC release), which dates the pairing.
efficacy.note: ASP6294 320 mg SC q4w missed the primary IC pain endpoint (LS mean -0.2, P=0.591); the arthritis-rodent data, public only in 2022, are a retrodiction that failed to reproduce it.
efficacy.quote: Analysis type superiority P-value = 0.591 Method MMRM Parameter type Least-Squares (LS) Mean Difference Point estimate -0.2
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction rule: the model's results were first public in 2022, after ASP6294's own IC result (EU CTR 2020-02-08) and tanezumab's IC results (2011-2012), so retrodiction true; it predicted analgesia and the trial missed, so contra stands. Paired by us: Koya 2023 reports only tolerability in IC/BPS. Dated 2022, when both sides were public.
efficacy.model: ASP6294 (PEG-Fab') vs anti-NGF IgG in adjuvant-arthritis mice and MIA-arthritis rats
Chemical cystitis in rats/mice with NGF sequestration
efficacy.note: Track opener: NGF-sequestration cystitis model (1997), later paired with fulranumab SC in IC/BPS.
efficacy.quote: Systemic treatment with the nerve growth factor-sequestering molecule, but not control molecules, partially and significantly reversed established inflammatory changes, by about 30-60%, depending on outcome measure.
efficacy.judgement: Opening untested entry for the chem-cystitis x fulranumab x sc track, at the model's first use (proxy).

efficacy.model: Chemical cystitis in rats/mice with NGF sequestration
efficacy.note: Fulranumab 9 mg SC at weeks 1, 5 and 9 did not beat placebo on average daily pain in IC/BPS (n=31 of 70 planned; stopped for the class hold).
efficacy.quote: In ANOVA analyses, there was no statistically significant difference between treatment groups for the primary endpoint (LS mean difference [95% CI] vs. placebo, -0.2 [-1.52, 1.10]) or any of the secondary endpoints.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. NCT01060254 posted no results; terminated for the FDA hold with 31 of 70 patients, so underpowered (the authors say so).
efficacy.judgement: Paired by us with the NGF-sequestration cystitis model (sibling sequestrant, product_in_model false). Primary endpoint missed, scored contra; the early stop is in confidence, not status.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: sign of change in bladder pain vs placebo

efficacy.model: Chemical cystitis in rats/mice with NGF sequestration
efficacy.note: Track opener: NGF-sequestration cystitis model (1997), later paired with ASP6294 SC in IC/BPS.
efficacy.quote: Systemic treatment with the nerve growth factor-sequestering molecule, but not control molecules, partially and significantly reversed established inflammatory changes, by about 30-60%, depending on outcome measure.
efficacy.judgement: Opening untested entry for the chem-cystitis x ASP6294 x sc track, at the model's first use (proxy).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: sign of change vs control (rat bladder reflexes vs IC daily pain NRS)
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry results record read (first posted 2020-02-08); women only.
efficacy.note: ASP6294 320 mg SC q4w did not beat placebo on the primary IC/BPS pain endpoint (LS mean -0.2, P=0.591), against the cystitis model.
efficacy.quote: Analysis type superiority P-value = 0.591 Method MMRM Parameter type Least-Squares (LS) Mean Difference Point estimate -0.2
efficacy.judgement: Split from entry 3, where ASP6294 sat in patient_trials: its own track on the NGF-sequestration cystitis model. Paired by us; the 1997 model predates the trial, so not a retrodiction.

safety.model: Primate, rat and mouse toxicology with bone and joint histology
safety.note: The IC POC saw headache and paresthesia, no joint signal; the toxicology package had not yet been compared with a patient outcome.
safety.short: Tox silent on joints; POC saw paresthesia
safety.quote: The most common adverse events were headache (tanezumab 20.6%, placebo 16.7%) and paresthesia (tanezumab 17.6%, placebo 3.3%).
safety.confidence_note: Abstract only. model_first_use_year 2008 is a proxy: the IC POC (NCT00601484) started 2008-03-17, and the tox package preceded it.
safety.judgement: The strip opens at the first IC safety readout, not at the proxy first-use year, because no source dates the toxicology studies.

safety.model: Primate, rat and mouse toxicology with bone and joint histology
safety.note: Imported-harm ruling: IC patients were measured, so they set the status. Tox predicted no joint harm; the IV IC POC logged no serious joint event (arthralgia 3/34 vs 0/30, non-serious). Model: Tanezumab or murine MuMAb911 in primate, rat and mouse for up to 6 months; hip and stifle histology, micro-CT, bone biomarkers: no adverse bone or joint change.
safety.short: Tox silent on joints; IC patients had none
safety.quote: The non-clinical investigations we have conducted found no evidence of an effect on the vasculature, bone, or joint in animals treated with large multiples of the clinical dose of tanezumab.
safety.confidence_note: Sponsor briefing hosted by FDA. IC side from NCT00601484 registry AEs (SAEs: none joint-related; non-serious arthralgia 3/34 vs 0/30, joint injury 1/34). Arthralgia is a symptom tox histology could not show. The SC IC trial (NCT00999518, posted 2021-08-03) logged one osteoarthritis SAE (2.5 mg), one arthralgia SAE and one bone-pain SAE on tanezumab vs none on placebo, unadjudicated: inconclusive, not split.
safety.reason: No serious joint event in IC patients
safety.judgement: Was contra on the RPOA seen in osteoarthritis patients (imported). The brief imports a harm only when this disease has no patient safety data for the class; IC patients were measured, no IC trial logged an adjudicated joint event, so the IC result sets the status: same. Tox package was filed under the IND before the IC trials (model_filed true), so not a retrodiction.
safety.magnitude_basis: presence vs absence of serious or structural joint events in IC patients
safety.population: Women and men with IC/BPS (tanezumab IV POC)

safety.confidence_note: Full text searched. model_first_use_year 2016 is a proxy (EudraCT 2016-004138-12).
safety.note: In MIA-arthritis rats an anti-NGF IgG promoted joint edema over time and ASP6294 did not; a lower joint-harm risk was predicted.
safety.quote: While the anti-NGF IgG promoted edema over time, the anti-NGF PEGylated Fab' did not.
safety.judgement: A different safety system from the draft's three-species toxicology: an IgG-vs-Fab' joint-edema comparison in arthritic rats, designed against the class's RPOA signal.
safety.model: ASP6294 (PEG-Fab') vs anti-NGF IgG in adjuvant-arthritis mice and MIA-arthritis rats

safety.magnitude_basis: presence vs absence of joint or serious adverse events
safety.confidence_note: Sponsor authors; the statement is global, not joint-specific, and a 12-week trial in ~56 dosed women without OA can barely show RPOA. EU CTR record lists 0/56 SAEs on ASP6294.
safety.note: Passing-tolerability and retrodiction rulings: Koya 2023 states ASP6294 was safe in IC/BPS (0/56 SAEs vs 3/61); the rat data were first public after that result, so retro.
safety.short: ASP6294 safe in IC/BPS as predicted
safety.quote: Phase 1 and Phase 2a clinical studies of anti-NGF Fab’-PEG (ASP6294) have been completed, and ASP6294 was well-tolerated and safe in healthy subjects and subjects with bladder pain syndrome/interstitial cystitis.
safety.reason: No harm seen; trial too small for RPOA
safety.judgement: The model's no-edema finding is a safety prediction and the sponsor's IC tolerability statement is its patient side. Safety is a drug claim: ASP6294's own IC safety result (EU CTR 2020-02-08) was public before the model (2022), so retrodiction; it matched, so retro. Low confidence: a 12-week trial with no IgG arm or joint imaging can barely test the joint claim (the checker's untested reading).
safety.model: ASP6294 (PEG-Fab') vs anti-NGF IgG in adjuvant-arthritis mice and MIA-arthritis rats

safety.population: Women and men with IC/BPS (tanezumab IV POC)
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. First use dated by publication (epub 2016-07-05); the experiments are undated.
safety.note: Rat medial meniscal tear model dosed with tanezumab, built to test whether it reproduces the RPOA seen in OA trials.
safety.short: Rat MMT built to model RPOA
safety.quote: To investigate whether the effects of nerve growth factor (NGF) inhibition with tanezumab on rats with medial meniscal tear (MMT) effectively model rapidly progressive osteoarthritis (RPOA) observed in clinical trials.
safety.judgement: Opening entry for a model run after tanezumab's IC and OA patient results were known; IC patients set the status (imported-harm ruling).
safety.model: Rat medial meniscal tear model dosed with tanezumab

safety.magnitude_basis: predicted cartilage damage vs no serious or structural joint event in IC patients
safety.population: Women and men with IC/BPS (tanezumab IV POC)
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; Pfizer authors. Quote from LaBranche 2017 (model side); IC side from Evans 2011 and NCT00601484 registry AEs. The model's harm needs an acutely injured, loaded joint, which IC patients lack, so the comparison is weak.
safety.note: Imported-harm ruling: IC patients set the status. The rat model predicts cartilage damage under tanezumab; IC patients on tanezumab IV showed no serious joint event, so the predicted harm did not appear.
safety.short: Predicts joint harm IC patients lacked
safety.quote: Prophylactic treatment with tanezumab prevented gait deficiency and resulted in more severe cartilage damage.
safety.reason: Post-hoc rat model; IC showed no RPOA
safety.judgement: Was retro against OA patients' RPOA (imported). IC patients were measured, so their result decides: the model's predicted joint damage did not appear in them. Retrodiction (model public 2016, after tanezumab's own IC safety data in 2011) that failed to reproduce it: contra, magnitude opposite.
safety.model: Rat medial meniscal tear model dosed with tanezumab
